name: Earth science: Atlantic hurricane intensity forecasting from the best track
description: Fit a statistical tropical-cyclone intensity model on the 1950-2014 Atlantic best track and forecast the 12-120 h maximum sustained wind for every advisory-time record of the held-out 2015-2024 storms. The score is the mean absolute intensity error over seven lead times.

sources.locator: Knaff et al. (2003): SHIFOR5, five-day statistical intensity forecasts from climatology and persistence.
Landsea and Franklin (2013): HURDAT2 format, content and best-track uncertainty.
HURDAT2 Atlantic best track, release of 4 April 2025 (1851-2024); public domain; the 1950-2024 synoptic records are used.
NHC 2024 forecast verification report: Tables 2 and 4 give 2019-2023 mean official, CLIPER5 and Decay-SHIFOR5 errors by lead.

requirements.datasets: Derived from pinned public sources by python3 scripts/prepare_earth.py (hashes in catalog/earth-data-lock.json).

evaluation.benchmark: Earth science: Atlantic hurricane intensity forecasting from the best track
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: fit_intensity_model(training_storms) -> model; model.forecast(history) -> float array (7,) of forecast maximum sustained 1-min 10-m winds (kt) at 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 120 h. Storms are dicts with read-only arrays time_hours (hours since 1950-01-01 00 UTC), month, day, hour, day_of_year, lat (deg N), lon (deg E, west negative), vmax_kt, mslp_hpa (NaN when missing), plus year (int) and status (tuple of HURDAT2 codes TD, TS, HU, EX, SD, SS, LO, WV, DB), one entry per 6-hourly synoptic record. training_storms are the 1950-2014 Atlantic HURDAT2 storms. Forecasts are requested in chronological order for every 6-hourly record of a held-out 2015-2024 storm at which it is TD/TS/HU/SD/SS and that verifies at one or more leads; history holds that storm's records up to and including the forecast time and nothing later. A lead verifies only if the storm is still TD/TS/HU/SD/SS at the verifying time (NHC convention). Score: mean over the seven leads of the mean absolute error (kt) against the best-track maximum wind; lower is better. Values outside [0, 300] kt, NaN or wrong shapes are invalid

limitations: Only best-track history is available (no sea-surface temperature, wind shear, land mask or forecast track), so rapid intensification and landfall decay can be anticipated only from history, date and position; official forecasts use far more information.
Best-track maximum winds are rounded to 5 kt and carry analysis uncertainty of roughly 10 kt or more for weaker systems (Landsea and Franklin 2013), which bounds achievable errors.
A better score is a better statistical intensity model on these seasons, not a scientific discovery.
The held-out observations are public, so search feedback on this fixed split can overfit it; freeze a candidate and test it on later or independent data before claiming a scientific improvement.
Candidate and evaluator share one Python process; the API withholds held-out data but is not a security sandbox.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value exists for this exact protocol. For context, NHC reports 2019-2023 mean Atlantic official intensity errors of 5.0, 7.3, 8.5, 9.7, 10.9, 12.9 and 15.5 kt at 12, 24, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 120 h and Decay-SHIFOR5 errors of 6.6, 10.2, 13.1, 15.6, 18.6, 21.8 and 22.6 kt on a different (operational, homogeneous) sample.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the maximum sustained wind of an Atlantic tropical cyclone one to five days ahead.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Intensity determines wind damage and storm-surge risk, and intensity forecasts have improved more slowly than track forecasts; climatology-and-persistence models define the skill baseline.

papers.title: Statistical, 5-Day Tropical Cyclone Intensity Forecasts Derived from Climatology and Persistence
papers.primary_goal: Develop and evaluate statistical five-day tropical cyclone intensity forecasts from climatology and persistence predictors.
papers.task_relation: The task scores the same kind of history-only intensity forecast against the best track at 12-120 h on the 2015-2024 Atlantic seasons; it does not reproduce the paper's samples or inland decay component.

science_relevance.reason: The cited paper's main goal is statistical tropical cyclone intensity prediction, the problem the local task scores; no reproduction of its numbers is claimed.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Crossref metadata and the NHC 2024 verification report (Decay-SHIFOR5 description and error tables) inspected; local evaluator run on the pinned HURDAT2 release.
